title: Security posture discovery - Verdigris Health
next_steps: Send SOC 2 Type II report and info sec packet (Ethan)
Share VPC/private deployment architecture doc and KMS/HSM options (Priya)
Schedule 1-week technical deep dive/baseline benchmark with Liam (w/c 2026-04-13)
action_items: Ethan Park - Send SOC2 + security whitepaper - 2026-04-09
Priya Nair - Share VPC diagram and KMS integration notes - 2026-04-10
Liam Chen - Provide list of compliance questions and sample network diagrams - 2026-04-12
summary: Intro discovery focused on Verdigris's compliance requirements for PHI, preference for private/VPC or on-prem options, SSO/SAML requirements, RBAC/audit logging expectations, encryption key management (KMS/HSM) and data retention policies. Redwood clarified hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs and committed to share SOC2 and technical docs and schedule a deeper technical benchmark.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Data residency and retention for PHI
questions: Do you support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS)?
What audit logging retention windows do you provide by default?
Can we run a Private/VPC deployment in our AWS account or on-prem?
How do you handle tokenization/PII redaction for model outputs?
What certification evidence can you provide (SOC2, ISO27001)?
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we really appreciate you taking the time. i'm ethan from redwood, with priya our solutions engineer. quick intros?
[00:07] Dr. Maya Reyes: Hi i'm maya i'm ciso at verdigris, we've got liam our cloud lead and rosa product.
[00:12] Liam Chen: hi all.
[00:14] Priya Nair: thanks, quick agenda is SOC2/ISO posture, auth/SSO, key management, and deployment options. we'll keep it interactive.
[00:22] Rosa Alvarez: sounds good, main driver is we need to add LLM features to our clinician workflow, lots of PHI. we need to understand whether hosted is possible or if we must do private.
[00:33] Ethan Park: totally. maybe start high level — what are your hard requirements? maya?
[00:37] Dr. Maya Reyes: hard requirements first: SOC2 type ii, we also prefer iso27001 but not mandatory, SSO via SAML (okta), strict RBAC -- least privilege, audit logs that are tamper-evident and retained for at least 7 years, encryption with customer-managed keys ideally HSM-backed, full control over data residency (us-east-1). also we need evidence for data flow to legal for audits.
[01:05] Priya Nair: ok that's helpful. for the audit logs, are you primarily concerned about access logs, model prompts/outputs, or both?
[01:13] Dr. Maya Reyes: both — we need a ledger of who called what model and full request/response metadata. actual PHI in outputs needs to be redacted or stored only if we control KMS.
[01:23] Liam Chen: to add, our security policy currently forbids vendor-managed keys for PHI in prod, so BYOK is a hard ask.
[01:30] Ethan Park: understood, BYOK for prod is a common ask for healthcare customers. Redwood has a few deployment modes — hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC or on-prem). each has different controls for keys and networking.
[01:43] Rosa Alvarez: can you give a short breakdown?
[01:45] Priya Nair: hosted is our fastest time to value — we manage everything, keys are managed by redwood. for customers with PHI it's usually not acceptable unless they have contractual exceptions, so hosted might be limited. dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and stricter tenant isolation but keys are still managed unless we pair with a private networking option. private (VPC/private control plane or on-prem) allows you to use your own KMS and put the runtime inside your VPC or even on-prem.
[02:12] Dr. Maya Reyes: that aligns with what we thought. for private in-vpc, is the control plane still in redwood? we need to avoid data plane egress.
[02:21] Priya Nair: good q. in our VPC option the control plane metadata calls home for billing/telemetry but we can sign an agreement to minimize telemetry. data plane can be configured to stay entirely in your VPC, no egress. we also have an air-gapped on-prem package if you need zero egress and full control.
[02:41] Liam Chen: great. for KMS, can we bring AWS KMS keys and have HSM-backed keys rotate under our policies?
[02:47] Ethan Park: yes — the private/VPC and on-prem options support BYOK with customer-managed KMS. we document key rotation and HSM options. we'll share the KMS integration guide after the call.
[02:56] Dr. Maya Reyes: what certifications can you provide right now?
[02:59] Priya Nair: we are SOC2 Type II compliant — we can share the latest report under NDA. we are working toward ISO27001 and can provide our security whitepaper, pen test summary and SOC2 attestation.
[03:11] Dr. Maya Reyes: good, we'll need the SOC2 report for procurement. is there a formal SSP and SSP evidence?
[03:16] Ethan Park: yes we can provide SSP artifacts, plus evidence packages for major controls — we'll send those.
[03:22] Rosa Alvarez: quick question on RBAC — does Redwood integrate with our existing SSO/SCIM for provisioning roles? we want automated role sync from Okta.
[03:31] Priya Nair: yes SAML for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning are supported. our RBAC maps IdP groups to roles and you can define least-privilege routes (e.g., admin, infra, analytics). we also support service accounts with scoped API keys and can limit by model/route.
[03:49] Liam Chen: do API keys still appear in logs? we prefer tokenized service accounts that don't leak secrets in logs.
[03:56] Priya Nair: we mask secrets in logs; service account tokens are hashed and only token identifiers show up in audit logs. full secrets are never logged.
[04:04] Dr. Maya Reyes: on audit logs, they need to be tamper-evident — WORM or similar. what do you store, how long, and who can access?
[04:13] Ethan Park: audit events are shipped to a customer-configurable sink — can be our managed log retention or forward to your S3/Cloudwatch in your account for long-term archival. retention defaults to 90 days on hosted but for enterprise/private we can customize up to multi-year retention and support WORM via S3 Object Lock or equivalent in your cloud.
[04:34] Liam Chen: so we could route logs to our S3 with object lock enabled and manage lifecycle to hit 7 years.
[04:39] Priya Nair: exactly. also we support streaming of structured audit events (JSON) including request ids, user ids, model id, and non-sensitive metadata. we avoid storing full PII in the logs unless you opt in.
[04:52] Rosa Alvarez: about model outputs — sometimes clinicians paste PHI into prompts. how do you recommend we manage that? redaction pre/post?
[05:00] Priya Nair: common patterns: client-side redaction before sending to Redwood, or using our prefix/KV caching to minimize storing sensitive prompts. for wholly private runs you can set policies to not persist inputs/outputs. we can also integrate a token redaction service in the pipeline.
[05:13] Dr. Maya Reyes: what about differential privacy or anonymization features?
[05:17] Priya Nair: not baked into the runtime as a single switch — we recommend a pre-processing step that tokenizes PHI or applies anonymization, then post-process to remap if needed. we have partners and examples for that.
[05:30] Ethan Park: moving to network controls, do you expect the runtime inside your AWS account or are you open to a hosted private space?
[05:36] Liam Chen: prefer inside our AWS account. procurement will likely refuse managed infra unless keys are BYOK and the runtime is within our VPC.
[05:44] Priya Nair: for VPC private deployment we deploy the runtime into your AWS account — you own the subnets, SGs, and can use your KMS. control plane can be on redwood side but we can limit metadata flow and put a proxy.
[05:58] Dr. Maya Reyes: are there any residual egresses, like model updates or kernel downloads?
[06:03] Priya Nair: model artifacts are pulled via secure channels; we can arrange a model pull flow that goes through your allowed endpoints, or we can provide an air-gapped bundle for on-prem.
[06:12] Liam Chen: what about runtime hardening — image signing, vulnerability scanning, and nightly patching?
[06:17] Priya Nair: we sign container images, run automated scanning, and provide SBOMs. for private/on-prem we can coordinate patch windows and provide signed updates.
[06:27] Rosa Alvarez: timeline — if we evaluate private, how long to stand up a VPC deployment for a POC?
[06:33] Ethan Park: typical POC setup for a VPC deployment is 2-4 weeks depending on approvals and networking rules. on-prem longer. we can do a lightweight dedicated trial faster but it won't meet your BYOK requirement.
[06:46] Liam Chen: we may want to start with a private POC for a single clinician workflow. can you support demo data that mimics PHI?
[06:53] Priya Nair: yes use anonymized synthetic data or a redacted dataset — we recommend synthetic for initial tests.
[06:58] Dr. Maya Reyes: procurement will ask for indemnities and data processing addendum; do you have a standard DPA and BAA?
[07:05] Ethan Park: we have a DPA and a BAA template for healthcare customers. we'll share redlines we've accepted previously to speed procurement.
[07:13] Rosa Alvarez: ok great. one last question on secrets: does the control plane ever hold plaintext keys?
[07:20] Priya Nair: no, control plane never stores customer KMS keys; only key references. crypto operations for data encryption happen in the data plane within your VPC when using BYOK.
[07:31] Liam Chen: ok, good. how about incident response and breach notification timelines?
[07:36] Ethan Park: we commit to notify within 72 hours of confirmed data breach and provide incident packs; for enterprise we can tighten SLAs contractually.
[07:45] Dr. Maya Reyes: can you run a quick demo of where audit logs live in the console?
[07:49] Priya Nair: quick screen share now? (brief pause) — showing the console, audit trail, filters by user/model/date — you can also export a JSON event stream.
[08:05] Rosa Alvarez: looking at the UI — can I filter out PII sensitive fields?
[08:09] Priya Nair: yes you can configure masking rules and sample redaction policies.
[08:15] Ethan Park: wrapping up, action items — we'll send SOC2 and security packet, priya will share KMS/VPC docs, and we'll set up a technical deep dive with liam. any blockers on dates?
[08:27] Liam Chen: week of april 13 works.
[08:30] Dr. Maya Reyes: we'll compile a list of compliance Qs and share by monday.
[08:34] Ethan Park: great. thanks everyone; we'll follow up with the packet and a calendar invite for the deep dive.
[08:39] Rosa Alvarez: thanks.
[08:41] (call ends)

Notes: transcription occasionally had minor mislabels; speakers interleaved. references: shared link to SOC2 via secure share to be sent; VPC/KMS integration doc (link to be attached in follow-up).
